data.long_meaning: The one who conquers or subdues. The name Fatanah carries the meaning “Conquering” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Fatanah usually hope their child will grow to embody conquering and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Fatanah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Conquering.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fatanah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: فطنة
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم فطنة مشتق من الفطام، يعني الذكاء الحاد والفهم السريع للامور، وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة البقرة الآية 269 'وَمَا يُؤتَى الذّكاءَ إِلّا أُوْلُواْ الأَلْبَابِ'، يدل على الشخص الذكي الذي يفهم بسرعة ويدرك الأمور بسهولة، ويحمل معنى روحي يعبر عن الحكمة والفطنة الربانية.

in_urdu.name: فطنة
in_urdu.meaning: تیز ذہانت اور جلدی سمجھنے کی صلاحیت
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام فطنة عربی زبان کی اصطلاح فطام سے نکلا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے تیز ذہانت اور جلدی سمجھنے کی صلاحیت، قرآن مجید میں سورة آل عمران الآية 191 'وَالذّكِرُ لِلذّكاءِ' میں اس کا ذکر آیا ہے، یہ نام ذہانت اور سمجھداری کی خصوصیت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے، جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے لئے یہ نام ثقافتی اور روحانی اہمیت رکھتا ہے.

in_english.name: Fatanah
in_english.long_meaning: The name Fatanah originates from the Arabic root 'f-ṭ-m', signifying intelligence, wisdom, and the ability to quickly comprehend and understand matters, referenced in the Quranic verse 'And none are given such insight except those with sound reason' (Quran 2:269), symbolizing sharp intellect and spiritual awareness, Fatanah is a name cherished across Muslim cultures for its profound meaning and significance.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Fatanah" holds deep cultural significance in Islamic history and traditions. It is derived from the Arabic root word "fatana," which means "to conquer" or "to subdue." Historically, the term has been used to describe individuals who have demonstrated remarkable strength, leadership, and courage in their military and political endeavors. In Islamic literature, Fatanah has been used as a name for powerful women warriors who fought bravely and successfully in various conflicts, inspiring others with their unwavering commitment and determination. The cultural impact of this name extends beyond military conquests, as it can also refer to anyone who overcomes their personal challenges and obstacles through courage, resilience, and perseverance.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Fatanah" also carries profound spiritual significance in Islamic tradition. It reminds us of the power of faith in enabling us to conquer our inner challenges and obstacles. The ultimate conquest is not just over external enemies, but also over the self and its desires. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said, "Conquer yourselves, for it is the strongest conquest." (Ibn Majah) Thus, the name Fatanah encourages us to embark on the spiritual journey of self-conquest, striving to purify our hearts, overcome our faults, and seek inner peace and tranquility. By embodying the qualities of courage, resilience, and determination, we can not only overcome the challenges of this world but also achieve spiritual growth and progress towards God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Conquering" symbolizes The one who conquers or subdues. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Fatanah serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of conquering.
